answer: Price each new identity on a rising cost ridge: bind every account to one scarce external anchor — a staked deposit of capital that cannot be rehypothecated — and make the required stake grow convexly with how many identities already trace back to that same anchor. The first agent is cheap; the tenth pays like a cedar sinking an ever-deeper taproot, super-linearly. A sybil operator spinning up a fleet thus faces roughly N-squared locked collateral, every unit slashable on a failed non-kin peer audit, so mass impersonation stops being affordable long before it ever buys voting weight.
